questions.prompt: The sequence f_n(x) = xⁿ converges uniformly on [0, 1].
questions.explanation: The pointwise limit is discontinuous at 1, while a uniform limit of continuous functions must be continuous.

questions.prompt: On which series can the Weierstrass M-test conclude uniform convergence on all of ℝ?
questions.explanation: |cos(nx)/n²| ≤ 1/n², and Σ 1/n² converges; the other bounds are not summable.

questions.prompt: A uniform limit of continuous functions is always ___. Give one word.
What is the radius of convergence of Σ xⁿ/2ⁿ?
questions.explanation: By the ratio test it converges when |x|/2 < 1, so R = 2.

questions.prompt: The power series Σ xⁿ/n has radius of convergence 1. At which of these points does it converge?
questions.explanation: At x = 1 it is the divergent harmonic series; at x = −1 it is the convergent alternating harmonic series; x = 2 lies outside the radius.

questions.prompt: A power series can be differentiated term by term inside its open interval of convergence.
questions.explanation: The differentiated series has the same radius of convergence and converges uniformly on compact subintervals.

questions.prompt: Match each concept to its meaning in a metric space.
pairs: Every sequence has a convergent subsequence
Cannot be split into two disjoint nonempty open sets
Every point has a ball contained in the set

questions.prompt: In ℝ² with the Euclidean metric, what is the distance between (1, 2) and (4, 6)?
ℚ with the usual metric is a complete metric space.
questions.explanation: A sequence of rationals converging to √2 is Cauchy in ℚ but has no limit in ℚ.

questions.prompt: For f(x, y) = (xy, x + y), what is the determinant of the Jacobian matrix at (3, 5)?
questions.explanation: J = [[y, x], [1, 1]] has determinant y − x = 5 − 3 = 2.

questions.prompt: If the second partial derivatives of f are continuous, then ∂²f/∂x∂y = ∂²f/∂y∂x.
The Inverse Function Theorem gives a local inverse of a C¹ map f at a point a provided what condition?
choices: The Jacobian matrix at a is invertible
All partial derivatives at a are zero
The Jacobian determinant at a is 0
questions.answer: The Jacobian matrix at a is invertible
questions.explanation: A nonzero Jacobian determinant means the linearization is invertible, which the theorem upgrades to a local inverse.

questions.prompt: What is the Lebesgue measure of ℚ ∩ [0, 1]?
questions.explanation: It is countable, and every countable set has measure zero.

questions.prompt: A σ-algebra is closed under complements and ___ unions. Give one word.
questions.explanation: Countable (not just finite) unions distinguish a σ-algebra from an algebra.

questions.prompt: Explain why the indicator function of ℚ ∩ [0, 1] is not Riemann integrable.
rubric: Every subinterval contains both rationals and irrationals
Upper sums are all 1 and lower sums are all 0
Concludes the upper and lower integrals differ
questions.model: Every subinterval of any partition contains both rationals and irrationals, so each upper sum is 1 and each lower sum is 0. The upper and lower integrals therefore differ (1 vs 0) and the Riemann integral does not exist.
questions.explanation: Dense rationals and irrationals force the sums apart.

questions.prompt: Which hypothesis does the Dominated Convergence Theorem require, in addition to pointwise convergence fₙ → f?
questions.explanation: A single integrable dominating function controls all fₙ and lets the limit pass inside the integral.

questions.prompt: What is the Lebesgue integral of the simple function 2·1_[0,3] + 5·1_[3,4]?
Every Riemann integrable function on [a, b] is Lebesgue integrable with the same integral.
questions.explanation: The Lebesgue integral extends the Riemann integral.
